title: Pumpkin Chowder with Toasted Pepitas
description: Author Steven Petusevsky: "This chowder is rich and full of bold tropical flavor. You can leave it chunky as I do, or purée it if you like it smooth and creamy. Sometimes I substitute 1 cup of the vegetable broth or water for a cup of light coconut milk for a bit of extra richness."
ingredients: 8 cup low sodium vegetable broth (or use water)
3 sprig fresh thyme (or 1 teaspoon dried thyme)
steps: Place squash, broth, tomatoes, onion, pepper, ginger root, scallions, and thyme sprigs or dried thyme in a nonreactive large saucepan. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until all ingredients are tender.
Add cilantro, lime juice, and salt. Remove thyme stems before serving. Garnish each bowl of soup with pepitas before serving. Makes about 2 quarts.

title: Roasted Pear Sauce
description: Instead of store-bought apple sauce, try simple, homemade pear sauce! Pears have a milder, sweeter flavor than apples. Roasting the pears before blending them into a sauce caramelizes their natural sugars for an even sweeter flavor.
ingredients: 3 large pear (about 1 1/2 lb, cored and cut in 1-inch pieces)
1 tbsp honey or 2 packets artificial sweetener
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.

In a large bowl, toss the pears with melted butter. Pour the pears into a baking dish and roast, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes or until pears are tender, stirring once or twice. Set the cooked pears aside to cool.
Add the pears back to the large bowl; add the honey and lemon juice. Using an immersion blender or stand up blender, blend the pear mixture until almost smooth. Stir in the walnuts.

title: Tomato and Basil Omelet
description: Start your day off with a savory Tomato and Basil Omelet. Incorporating egg whites helps lower the saturated fat while fresh tomato and basil add in a punch of color and flavor.
steps: Whisk the eggs in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a small non-stick pan over medium heat.
Pour the beaten eggs into the pan.
Sprinkle diced tomato and chopped basil on half the omelet.
Once the eggs are set, fold the omelet in half and cook until the tomato softens, about 30 seconds.

title: Coastal Sancocho
description: Sancocho is a type of latin american stew made with meat and root vegetables. This recipe uses heart-healthy fish instead of beef for a flavorful dish that is low is saturated fat.
ingredients: 1/2 lbs fillet of sole (cut into bite-sized pieces)
1/2 lbs firm-fleshed white fish (such as halibut, sea, bass, or cod) (cut into bite-sized pieces)
2 whole potatoes (peeled and cut into chunks)
1 lbs cassava (yuca) (peeled and cut into 4 pieces)
1 tbsp plus 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro (divided use)
1/4 cup finely chopped sweet or hot red pepper
1 med onion (peeled and finely chopped, divided use)
steps: Combine the other half of the onion and 1/2 cup cilantro in small bowl. Garnish each soup serving with 1 Tbsp mixture.
Add potatoes, carrots, plantain, fish, and lime juice and simmer for 15 minutes. Add peas and cabbage and simmer 5 minutes.
Add cassava and milk, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Heat oil in large stockpot and sauté 1/2 of the onion, garlic, pepper, and 1 Tbsp cilantro for 3–4 minutes. Add clam juice and water and bring to a boil.

title: Orange and Apple Bars
description: These bars, with their thin layer of tasty apple butter, are a delightful snack or dessert. The crust is made with heart-healthy oats to boost the fiber.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly spray an 8-inch square baking dish with cooking spray.
In a medium bowl, stir together the oatmeal, flour, sugar, cardamom, nutmeg, and baking soda.
In a small bowl, using a fork, lightly beat the egg whites. Stir in the oil and 2 tbsp fresh orange juice.
Add the egg white mixture to the oatmeal mixture, stirring until the combined mixture holds together. Press three-fourths of the mixture into the baking dish.

In a medium bowl, whisk together the fruit butter and 2 tsp of the orange zest. Using a rubber scraper, spread the fruit butter mixture over the oatmeal mixture. Sprinkle with the remaining oatmeal mixture.
Bake for 30–35 minutes, or until the top is golden brown. Transfer the dish to a cooling rack and let cool completely, then cut into 24 equal bars.

title: Cottage Cheese and Veggie Wrap
description: Try a new way to eat cottage cheese with these delicious and easy Cottage Cheese and Veggie Wraps. If you want to add a punch of flavor, try drizzling on a bit of balsamic glaze before rolling up the wraps.
ingredients: 1 cup cottage cheese (no salt added, low fat)
1/4 cup fresh herbs (such as dill, basil, parsley, chopped)
steps: Lay out the tortillas on a clean surface.
Evenly spread the cottage cheese on each tortilla.
Distribute the cherry tomatoes, cucumber slices, red onion, and bell peppers over the cottage cheese.
Sprinkle the fresh herbs on top.
Season with the salt and pepper.
Fold in the sides of the tortillas and then roll them up tightly to create wraps.

title: Corn Casserole
description: Enjoy our diabetes-friendly corn casserole, a rich and creamy blend of sweet corn, creamy goodness, creating a warm and hearty dish that's perfect for family gatherings or cozy nights in.
ingredients: 2 (15 oz) cans Canned corn (Whole kernel, drained)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
In a large bowl, combine the whole kernel corn, cream-style corn, cornmeal, diced tomato, Greek yogurt, melted butter, honey, baking powder, salt, and pepper. Mix until well combined.
Pour the corn mixture into the prepared baking dish, spreading it evenly.
Bake for 45 minutes or until the top is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Remove the casserole from the oven.
Garnish with chopped fresh chives, if desired.
Allow the casserole to cool for a few minutes before serving.
